# Designing this blog

This folder is a complete blog for **folderblog**. Posts are Markdown files; the
engine turns them into a data model; **`theme/` decides every byte of the site**.
You can change anything in `theme/` without touching the engine. There is no
hidden base theme: if a file is not in `theme/`, it does not exist.

## The only rules the engine enforces

1. The engine owns: content discovery, Markdown rendering, post/page URLs, gallery URLs and image resizing,
   `/feed.xml` (RSS, full content, absolute URLs) and `/sitemap.xml`.
   A theme cannot produce those two paths; link to them with `site.feed_url`.
2. The engine never adds markup, classes, styles or scripts to theme output.
   (Only `folderblog preview` injects a live-reload `<script>`, and only while serving.)
3. Two outputs on one path is a build error that names both producers.
4. Never edit `posts/`, `pages/` or `drafts/` to make a design work. Those are the
   author's writing. Use `folderblog preview --fixtures stress` to test edge cases instead.

## How `theme/` becomes the site

- Any path with a segment starting with `_` (`_layouts/`, `_partials/`, `_macros/`,
  `_markup/`) is never output. Use it for templates you extend, include or import.
- Files ending in `.html` / `.htm` are **templates**, rendered to the same path
  (`theme/about.html` → `/about.html`, `theme/index.html` → `/`).
- Files ending in `.jinja` are templates rendered with the suffix removed
  (`theme/search.json.jinja` → `/search.json`, `theme/style.css.jinja` → `/style.css`,
  `theme/logo.svg.jinja` → `/logo.svg`).
- Every other file is copied byte for byte (`theme/assets/site.css` → `/assets/site.css`).
  Dotfiles are skipped except `.well-known/`, `.htaccess` and `.nojekyll`.
- Templates are Jinja (minijinja): `extends`, `block`, `include`, `import`/`macro`,
  `set`, `for … else`, `if`, `filter`, `with`, loop variables. Template names are paths
  relative to `theme/`: `{% extends "_layouts/base.html" %}`.
  Python-style string/list/dict methods work: `.startswith()`, `.split()`, `.items()`, `.get()`.
- Imported macros (`{% import %}` / `{% from … import %}`) can read the page context
  (`site`, `posts`, `item`…). Macros only output text; to "return" a value, output it and
  `| trim` it, or compute it with `{% set %}` in the caller.
- Every URL the engine gives you (`item.url`, `files[].url`, `older/newer.url`, `pager.*`,
  `site.url`, `site.feed_url`) already includes the base path. Use `| url` only on paths
  you write yourself. Use `item.permalink` for `<link rel="canonical">` and OpenGraph.
- Autoescaping is on for outputs ending in `.html`, `.htm`, `.xml`, `.svg`, `.rss`, `.atom`,
  and off for everything else (JSON, CSS, JS, text). In JSON use `| tojson`.
- Undefined values are lenient: `{{ post.meta.cover.url }}` is empty if `cover` is missing,
  and `{% if post.meta.cover %}` is false. `none` also prints as nothing. `folderblog check` warns when a template
  prints an undefined value, which is usually a typo.

### Posts and pages

- Each post renders `theme/_layouts/<layout>.html` at `post.url`; `layout` defaults to
  `post`. Pages default to `page`. Front matter `layout: photo` uses `_layouts/photo.html`,
  so one post can look unrelated to the next. A missing layout is a build error.
- In a layout, the item is `post` (or `page`) and also `item`.
- An `.html` file in `pages/` is itself a template, rendered with the full context at
  its page URL (it may `{% extends %}` theme templates). Use it for one-off designed pages.

### Route headers: one template, many pages

A template may start with a route header, a Jinja comment containing TOML:

```jinja
{#---
each = "tags"
as = "tag"
url = "/tags/{{ tag.slug }}/"
---#}
{% extends "_layouts/base.html" %}
{% block main %}<h1>{{ tag.name }}</h1>…{% endblock %}
```

| name | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | template string | Output URL for each rendered page. Ends in `/` for `<url>/index.html`. May use `item`, the `as` name, `pager.number`, and all globals. |
| `each` | expression | Render once per element of this Jinja expression, e.g. `tags` or `posts \| selectattr("meta.series") \| groupby("meta.series")`. |
| `as` | name | Extra variable name for the current element of `each` (it is always also `item`). |
| `paginate` | expression | Split this list into pages; each page gets `pager`. Can be combined with `each` (paginate per tag). |
| `per_page` | int | Items per page for `paginate` (default 10). |

The route header decides the output URL completely; where the template file sits in
`theme/` does not matter (`theme/year.html` with `url = "/{{ item.year }}/"` is fine).
`paginate` and `url` can use the `as` name (`paginate = "tag.posts"`).
Without a header, a template renders once at its mirrored path. With only `url`, it
renders once at that URL (`theme/archive.html` with `url = "/archive/"` → `/archive/`).
With `paginate` and no `each`, page 1 is at `url` rendered with `pager.number = 1`:

```jinja
{#---
paginate = "posts"
per_page = 10
url = "{% if pager.number == 1 %}/{% else %}/page/{{ pager.number }}/{% endif %}"
---#}
```

`each` accepts any expression over the context, so a theme can make collections the
engine has never heard of:

- per tag: `each = "tags"`
- per year: `each = "years"`, `url = "/{{ item.year }}/"`
- per series (front matter `series:`): `each = "posts | selectattr('meta.series') | groupby('meta.series')"`,
  then `item.grouper` is the series name and `item.list` its posts
- per data record: `each = "data.projects"`
- paginated per tag: `each = "tags"` plus `paginate = "item.posts"`, with a `url` that
  uses both `item.slug` and `pager.number`

### Controlling Markdown output

Optional templates override how body Markdown renders. Each one receives only the
variables listed plus `site` and `item` (`{slug, url, source, kind}` of the post or page
being rendered); if a file is absent the engine's plain HTML is used. Output is inserted
inline, so trailing newlines are trimmed; use inline elements (e.g. `<span>`, not
`<figure>`) in image and link overrides, since Markdown images sit inside a `<p>`.
Raw HTML written in a post (`<img>`, `<figure>`) passes through untouched and does
**not** go through these overrides.

- `theme/_markup/image.html` — `url`, `alt`, `title`, `index` (1 for the item's first image, 2 for the next…) — replaces `<img>` for Markdown images
- `theme/_markup/link.html` — `url`, `title`, `text`, `html` (inner markup, safe), `external` (bool) — replaces `<a>`
- `theme/_markup/heading.html` — `level`, `id`, `text`, `html` (inner markup, safe), `classes` — replaces `<hN>`
- `theme/_markup/codeblock.html` — `lang`, `code` (highlighted HTML, safe), `raw` (plain source) — replaces `<pre><code>`

Code blocks without an override render as
`<pre class="highlight"><code class="language-LANG">` with `<span class="hl-…">` tokens
(classes only, never inline colours; the class names are TextMate scope atoms prefixed
with `hl-`, e.g. `hl-keyword`, `hl-string`, `hl-comment`, `hl-entity`, `hl-constant`,
`hl-storage`, `hl-support`, `hl-variable`, `hl-punctuation`). Headings get unique `id`s.
Raw HTML in Markdown is passed through. Footnotes, tables, task lists and
strikethrough are enabled. Relative image/link paths in a post (Markdown or raw HTML
`src`/`href`) are rewritten to site URLs; for paths in front matter use `resolve_url`.

Fixed body markup you may want to style:

- Heading ids are unique **within one item** only. If a page shows several items' full
  content, namespace them in `_markup/heading.html`, e.g. `id="{{ item.slug }}--{{ id }}"`.
- Footnotes: `<sup class="footnote-ref"><a href="#fn-SLUG-LABEL" id="fn-SLUG-ref-LABEL">1</a></sup>`
  and `<div class="footnote" id="fn-SLUG-LABEL"><span class="footnote-number">1</span>…<a class="footnote-back" href="#fn-SLUG-ref-LABEL">↩</a></div>`,
  where SLUG is the item's slug, so ids never collide across items.
- Tables: plain `<table><thead><tbody>`; column alignment written in Markdown (`:---:`)
  becomes `style="text-align: …"` on cells — the only inline style in body output.
- Task lists: `<input disabled type="checkbox">` inside `<li>`.

## The photo gallery

When blog.toml has `[gallery] enabled = true`, every JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF in `gallery/`
becomes a photo with its own page. The engine owns the gallery's URLs, like post URLs;
the theme owns every byte of how it looks:

| URL | template | variables |
|---|---|---|
| `gallery.url` | `theme/_gallery/index.html` | `gallery` (also `item`) |
| `<gallery.url><album>/` | `theme/_gallery/album.html` | `album` |
| `<gallery.url>tags/<tag>/` | `theme/_gallery/tag.html` | `tag` (a gallery tag) |
| `<gallery.url>[<album>/]<photo>/` | `theme/_gallery/photo.html` | `photo` |

All four must exist while the gallery is on (`folderblog gallery on` copies the default
ones in; it never overwrites). They are ordinary templates: extend `_layouts/base.html`,
include partials, import macros. `gallery` is a global on every page, so the site's
navigation can link to it with `{% if gallery.enabled %}`.

- Folders directly inside `gallery/` are albums (deeper folders belong to their album).
  An album's optional `index.md` gives it a title, `date`, `tags`, `cover: file.jpg`,
  `order: newest` and a description (its body).
- A sidecar `sunset.md` (or `sunset.jpg.md`) beside `sunset.jpg` gives the photo a title
  (front matter or leading heading), a caption (its body), `tags`, `date`, `alt`, `slug`,
  `draft`, and any other keys (in `photo.meta`). Photos need no sidecar.
- `gallery/index.md` gives the gallery its title and intro.
- Only resized, re-encoded copies are published (`photo.image`, `photo.thumb`), never the
  original files, so camera metadata such as GPS location never reaches the site.
  Resizing happens once per file and is cached in `.blog/`.
- Photo tags are separate from post tags. A tag page can still find posts with the same
  tag: `{% for t in tags if t.slug == tag.slug %}…{% endfor %}`.
- HEIC/AVIF/RAW files are skipped with a warning (export them as JPEG).

## Template context

Every template sees these globals:

| name | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `site` | object | Site settings from blog.toml; see **site** below. |
| `params` | object | The free-form `[params]` table from blog.toml (same as `site.params`). |
| `posts` | list of item | All published posts, newest first. In `preview` this also includes drafts (with `draft = true`). |
| `pages` | list of item | All pages, sorted by front matter `weight` (default 0) then title. |
| `tags` | list of tag | Every tag used by a post, sorted by name. |
| `years` | list of year | Posts grouped by year, newest year first. |
| `data` | object | Parsed files from `data/`: `data/links.toml` is `data.links`; subfolders nest (`data/a/b.json` is `data.a.b`). |
| `preview` | bool | True in `folderblog preview` (drafts visible), false in real builds. |
| `current_url` | string | URL of the file being rendered, e.g. `/2024/05/hello/` (includes the base path). |
| `current_path` | string | Output file being rendered, e.g. `2024/05/hello/index.html`. |
| `template` | string | The template file producing this output, e.g. `theme/_layouts/post.html`. |
| `item` | item or any | Posts/pages: the item being rendered. Routed templates with `each`: the current element. |
| `post` | item | Set when rendering a post (same value as `item`). |
| `page` | item | Set when rendering a page (same value as `item`). |
| `pager` | pager | Set in templates whose route header has `paginate`; see **pager** below. |
| `gallery` | gallery | The photo gallery; see **gallery** below. Always defined, so navigation can use `{% if gallery.enabled %}`. |
| `photo` | photo | Set when rendering `theme/_gallery/photo.html` (same value as `item`). |
| `album` | album | Set when rendering `theme/_gallery/album.html` (same value as `item`). |

### site

| name | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | `title` from blog.toml. |
| `description` | string | `description` from blog.toml (may be empty). |
| `author` | string | `author` from blog.toml (may be empty). |
| `language` | string | `language` from blog.toml, e.g. `en`. Use it for `<html lang>`. |
| `base_url` | string | Absolute site URL without trailing slash, e.g. `https://example.com`. |
| `base_path` | string | Path part of base_url (`""` for a site at the domain root, `/blog` for a subfolder site). |
| `url` | string | URL of the home page (`/`, or `/blog/` for a subfolder site). |
| `feed_url` | string | URL of the engine's RSS feed (`/feed.xml`). |
| `feed_url_absolute` | string | Absolute URL of the RSS feed. |
| `sitemap_url` | string | URL of the engine's sitemap (`/sitemap.xml`). |
| `params` | object | The `[params]` table from blog.toml. |
| `updated` | date or none | Date of the newest post. Deterministic, so output only changes when content does. |
| `generator` | string | `folderblog <version>`. |

### item (every post and page)

| name | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string | `"post"` or `"page"`. |
| `title` | string | Front matter `title`, else the leading heading (removed from `content`), else the filename. |
| `slug` | string | From the filename (date prefix removed) or bundle folder name; front matter `slug` overrides. |
| `url` | string | Site URL of the item, e.g. `/2024/05/hello/`. Use this in links. |
| `permalink` | string | Absolute URL, e.g. `https://example.com/2024/05/hello/`. |
| `date` | date or none | RFC 3339 string. Posts always have one; pages only if front matter sets `date`. |
| `date_source` | string or none | `front_matter`, `filename`, or `first_seen` (when the engine first saw the post). |
| `year` | int or none | Year of `date`. |
| `month` | int or none | Month of `date` (1-12). |
| `day` | int or none | Day of `date`. |
| `updated` | date or none | Front matter `updated` (or `modified`/`lastmod`), if set. |
| `content` | html | Rendered body HTML (already safe; do not escape). |
| `excerpt` | html | Front matter `excerpt`/`summary` rendered, else everything before `<!--more-->`, else the first paragraph. |
| `summary` | string | Plain-text version of `excerpt`, at most ~300 characters. |
| `has_more` | bool | True if the body contains a `<!--more-->` marker. |
| `raw` | string | The Markdown (or HTML page) source without front matter. |
| `text` | string | Plain text of the whole body (for search indexes). |
| `word_count` | int | Words in `text`. |
| `reading_time` | int | Minutes at 220 words per minute, at least 1. |
| `tags` | list of {name, slug} | From front matter `tags` (a list or a comma-separated string). |
| `headings` | list of {level, id, text} | Every heading in the body, in order, with its anchor id (for a table of contents). |
| `meta` | object | All front matter exactly as written, including keys the engine does not know about. |
| `draft` | bool | True for files in `drafts/` or with `draft: true` (only ever visible in preview). |
| `layout` | string | Layout name: front matter `layout`, else `post` or `page`. Renders `theme/_layouts/<layout>.html`. |
| `source` | string | Source file relative to the blog folder, e.g. `posts/hello.md`. |
| `older` | link or none | Posts only: the next older post as {title, url, slug, date}. |
| `newer` | link or none | Posts only: the next newer post as {title, url, slug, date}. |
| `files` | list of file | Files beside a bundle's `index.md`, as {name, url, ext, is_image}. Empty for single-file items. |

### tag

| name | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | Tag as first written. |
| `slug` | string | URL-safe form. The theme decides tag page URLs, e.g. `/tags/{{ tag.slug }}/`. |
| `count` | int | Number of posts. |
| `posts` | list of item | Posts with this tag, newest first. |

### year

| name | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `year` | int | The year. |
| `count` | int | Number of posts. |
| `posts` | list of item | Posts from that year, newest first. |

### pager

| name | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `number` | int | Current page number, starting at 1. |
| `total` | int | Number of pages (at least 1, even for an empty list). |
| `per_page` | int | Items per page. |
| `total_items` | int | Length of the whole list. |
| `items` | list | The items on this page. |
| `prev` | string or none | URL of the previous page. |
| `next` | string or none | URL of the next page. |
| `first` | string | URL of page 1. |
| `last` | string | URL of the last page. |
| `urls` | list of string | URLs of every page, in order. |

### gallery

| name | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | bool | `[gallery] enabled` from blog.toml. When false every list below is empty and no gallery pages are made. |
| `title` | string | Title of `gallery/index.md` (front matter or leading heading), else `Gallery`. |
| `url` | string | URL of the gallery page, from `[gallery] url` (default `/gallery/`). |
| `permalink` | string | Absolute URL of the gallery page. |
| `intro` | html | Body of `gallery/index.md`, rendered (empty if there is none). |
| `meta` | object | Front matter of `gallery/index.md`. |
| `count` | int | Number of photos. |
| `photos` | list of photo | Every photo, newest first (album photos included). |
| `albums` | list of album | Albums (folders inside `gallery/`), newest first. Empty folders are left out. |
| `tags` | list of gallery tag | Every tag used by a photo, sorted by name. Separate from the post `tags`. |

### photo

| name | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string | `"photo"`. |
| `title` | string | Sidecar front matter `title`, else its leading heading, else the filename. Empty for camera filenames (`IMG_2041`, `PXL_…`, `DSC…`). |
| `alt` | string | Sidecar `alt`, else the title, else the caption as text. May be empty. |
| `slug` | string | From the filename (date prefix removed); sidecar `slug` overrides. Unique within its album. |
| `url` | string | URL of the photo's own page, e.g. `/gallery/paris/eiffel/`. |
| `permalink` | string | Absolute URL of the photo's page. |
| `image` | string | URL of the published image: at most 2048 px on the long side, re-encoded so no EXIF or GPS data is published. GIFs are published unchanged. |
| `thumb` | string | URL of a thumbnail that fits in 1600×560 px (use it in grids). |
| `width` | int | Width of `image` in pixels (after applying the camera's rotation). |
| `height` | int | Height of `image` in pixels. |
| `thumb_width` | int | Width of `thumb`. |
| `thumb_height` | int | Height of `thumb`. |
| `ratio` | float | `width / height`, for aspect-ratio layouts (`style="--r: {{ photo.ratio }}"`). |
| `caption` | html | The sidecar's Markdown body, rendered (empty without a sidecar). |
| `date` | date | Sidecar `date`, else a `YYYY-MM-DD-` filename prefix, else when the camera took it (EXIF), else when folderblog first saw the file. |
| `date_source` | string | `front_matter`, `filename`, `exif` or `first_seen`. |
| `year` | int | Year of `date`. |
| `month` | int | Month of `date`. |
| `day` | int | Day of `date`. |
| `tags` | list of {name, slug, url} | Sidecar `tags` plus the album's `tags`; `url` is the gallery tag page. |
| `album` | {title, slug, url} or none | The album the photo is in. |
| `exif` | object or none | Camera settings as display strings, each possibly none: `camera`, `lens`, `focal_length` (`35 mm`), `aperture` (`ƒ/2.8`), `shutter` (`1/250 s`), `iso` (`ISO 200`). Location is never read. |
| `meta` | object | All sidecar front matter as written. |
| `draft` | bool | Sidecar `draft: true` (only ever visible in preview). |
| `source` | string | The image file, e.g. `gallery/paris/eiffel.jpg`. |
| `sidecar` | string or none | The sidecar file, e.g. `gallery/paris/eiffel.md`. |
| `prev` | {title, alt, url, thumb} or none | Previous photo in the same album (or among photos outside albums). |
| `next` | {title, alt, url, thumb} or none | Next photo in the same album (or among photos outside albums). |

### album

| name | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string | `"album"`. |
| `title` | string | Title of the album's `index.md`, else the folder name. |
| `slug` | string | From the folder name; `index.md` `slug` overrides. |
| `url` | string | URL of the album page, e.g. `/gallery/paris/`. |
| `permalink` | string | Absolute URL of the album page. |
| `description` | html | Body of the album's `index.md`, rendered. |
| `date` | date or none | `index.md` `date`, else the newest photo's date. |
| `cover` | photo | The photo named by `index.md` `cover: file.jpg`, else the album's first photo. |
| `photos` | list of photo | Oldest first (a story in order); `order: newest` in `index.md` reverses it. |
| `count` | int | Number of photos. |
| `tags` | list of {name, slug, url} | `index.md` `tags`; every photo in the album gets them too. |
| `meta` | object | Front matter of the album's `index.md`. |
| `source` | string | The folder, e.g. `gallery/paris/`. |

### gallery tag

| name | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string | `"tag"`. |
| `name` | string | Tag as first written. |
| `slug` | string | URL-safe form. |
| `url` | string | URL of the tag's gallery page, `<gallery.url>tags/<slug>/`. |
| `count` | int | Number of photos. |
| `photos` | list of photo | Photos with this tag, newest first. |

### Filters

folderblog filters:

- `date` — `{{ post.date | date("%B %-d, %Y") }}` — strftime format (default `%Y-%m-%d`). Accepts RFC 3339 or `YYYY-MM-DD` strings, or `"now"`.
- `url` — `{{ "/assets/site.css" | url }}` — prefix the site's base path to a site-absolute path. Use for every hand-written link so the theme works in a subfolder site.
- `absolute_url` — `{{ post.url | absolute_url }}` — full URL with scheme and host.
- `slugify` — `{{ "Hello World" | slugify }}` → `hello-world`.
- `markdown` — Render a Markdown string (e.g. a front matter field or data value) to HTML.
- `truncate_words` — `{{ post.summary | truncate_words(30) }}` — strip tags and cut to N words with an ellipsis.
- `plaintext` — Strip HTML tags and collapse whitespace.
- `striptags` — Strip HTML tags.
- `truncate` — `truncate(length=80)` — **keyword arguments only** (`length`, `killwords`, `end`, `leeway`); cuts at a word boundary. For an exact cut use slicing: `text[:80]`.
- `resolve_url` — `{{ post.meta.cover | resolve_url(post) }}` — resolve a path written in front matter exactly like a path in the body: relative to the item's file, then to where that file is published (bundle file, loose file, or another post's `.md`). Absolute URLs pass through; `/x` gets the base path.
- `wordcount` — Number of words in a string.
- `pluralize` — `{{ n }} post{{ n | pluralize }}`.
- `filesizeformat` — Human-readable byte size.

Standard filters (this is the complete list — Jinja2 filters not named here, such as
`xmlattr`, `center` or `wordwrap`, do not exist): `abs`, `attr`, `batch`, `bool`, `capitalize`, `chain`, `count`, `d`, `default`, `dictsort`, `e`, `escape`, `first`, `float`, `format`, `groupby`, `indent`, `int`, `items`, `join`, `last`, `length`, `lines`, `list`, `lower`, `map`, `max`, `min`, `pprint`, `reject`, `rejectattr`, `replace`, `reverse`, `round`, `safe`, `select`, `selectattr`, `slice`, `sort`, `split`, `string`, `sum`, `title`, `tojson`, `trim`, `unique`, `upper`, `urlencode`, `wordcount`, `zip`.

Tests (`x is …`): `defined`, `undefined`, `none`, `true`, `false`, `boolean`, `number`, `integer`, `float`, `string`, `sequence`, `mapping`, `iterable`, `odd`, `even`, `eq`, `ne`, `lt`, `le`, `gt`, `ge`, `in`, `sameas`, `safe`, `escaped`, `startingwith`, `endingwith`, `filter`, `test`.

### Functions

- `now` — `now()` — current time as an RFC 3339 string. Avoid in real output: it changes every build and forces a redeploy.
- `range` — Jinja `range(n)`.
- `dict` — Jinja `dict(a=1)`.
- `namespace` — Jinja `namespace()` for values that change inside loops.
- `cycler` — Jinja `cycler("odd", "even")`.
- `joiner` — Jinja `joiner(", ")`.

Dates are RFC 3339 strings; format them with `| date(...)`. Sort with
`posts | sort(attribute="title")`, filter with `posts | selectattr("meta.featured")`,
group with `posts | groupby("year")`.

## Content the templates will receive

- `posts/*.md` or `posts/<slug>/index.md` (a bundle: images beside it are published with
  it and listed in `item.files`). Subfolders without `index.md` are just organisation.
  Other files in `posts/` outside bundles are published at their own path
  (`posts/cover.svg` → `/posts/cover.svg`); in `pages/`, at the path below `pages/`
  (`pages/me.jpg` → `/me.jpg`). `resolve_url` knows all of this.
- Tags whose names give the same slug (`C++` and `c`) are merged; `check` warns about it.
- `pages/about.md` → `/about/`, `pages/projects/x.md` → `/projects/x/`, `pages/index.md` → `/`.
- `drafts/` — only in `preview`.
- `static/` — copied to the site root untouched (favicons, CNAME, downloads).
- `gallery/` — pictures for the photo gallery, when it is on (see **The photo gallery**).
- `data/` — JSON/TOML/YAML exposed as `data`.
- Front matter is optional (YAML between `---` or TOML between `+++`). Known keys:
  `title`, `date`, `tags`, `slug`, `layout`, `draft`, `excerpt`/`summary`, `updated`,
  `url` (override the output URL), `weight` (page order). Everything else passes through
  to `item.meta`, so a theme can invent its own keys (`cover`, `subtitle`, `color`…).

## blog.toml

| name | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | Site title (required). |
| `base_url` | string | Absolute URL the site is served from (required). May include a path for subfolder sites. |
| `description` | string | Used by the feed and available to templates. |
| `author` | string | Used by the feed and available to templates. |
| `language` | string | Default `en`. |
| `permalink` | string | Post URL pattern; tokens `{year}` `{month}` `{day}` `{slug}`. Default `/{year}/{month}/{slug}/`. |
| `feed.limit` | int | Number of posts in `/feed.xml` (default 20). |
| `build.pre` | list of commands | Shell commands run before a build (working directory: the blog folder). |
| `build.post` | list of commands | Shell commands run after rendering, with `$FOLDERBLOG_OUT` set to the fresh output directory; they may add or change files there. |
| `watch.ignore` | list of paths | Paths (relative to the blog folder, prefix match) whose changes never trigger a rebuild. |
| `gallery.enabled` | bool | Publish the pictures in `gallery/` as a photo gallery (default false). `folderblog gallery on` sets it and adds `gallery/` and the templates. |
| `gallery.url` | string | Where the gallery lives (default `/gallery/`). |
| `deploy.type` | string | `github`, `git` or `command`. |
| `deploy.owner` | string | github: account or org that owns the repo (set by `folderblog new` when logged in). |
| `deploy.repo` | string | github: repo name. Created, with Pages turned on, at the first deploy. |
| `deploy.domain` | string | github: optional custom domain; written as CNAME and set on Pages. Point your DNS at GitHub and set `base_url` to match. |
| `deploy.private` | bool | github: create the repo private (Pages on private repos needs a paid GitHub plan). |
| `deploy.remote` | string | git: remote URL or path. |
| `deploy.branch` | string | git, github: branch to push (default `gh-pages`). |
| `deploy.nojekyll` | bool | git: add an empty `.nojekyll` to the pushed tree (default true). |
| `deploy.author_name` | string | git: commit author name (default `folderblog`). |
| `deploy.author_email` | string | git: commit author email. |
| `deploy.command` | string | command: shell command; `$FOLDERBLOG_OUT` is the directory to publish. |
| `params` | table | Anything you like; exposed to templates as `site.params` and `params`. |

## Commands (run from the blog folder, or pass its path)

- `folderblog new [NAME] [--root] [--domain] [--repo] [--no-github]` — Create a new blog folder with the default theme and AGENTS.md (published to GitHub Pages if logged in)
- `folderblog login [SERVICE] [--client-id]` — Log in to GitHub so blogs can be published to GitHub Pages with no manual setup
- `folderblog logout [SERVICE]` — Forget the stored GitHub login
- `folderblog build [BLOG] [--out] [--drafts] [--fixtures]` — Build the blog into .blog/public (or --out) without deploying
- `folderblog preview [BLOG] [--port] [--fixtures FIXTURES]` — Serve a live-reloading local preview, drafts included
- `folderblog check [BLOG] [--fixtures FIXTURES]` — Render everything and report template errors, feed problems, broken links, collisions
- `folderblog data [URL] [--blog] [--drafts] [--fixtures]` — Print the exact template context for a URL as JSON (no URL: list all outputs)
- `folderblog watch [--root]` — Watch every blog under the root; rebuild and deploy on change
- `folderblog deploy [BLOG] [--force]` — Build and deploy a blog now
- `folderblog status [--root] [--json]` — Show build/deploy status for every blog under the root
- `folderblog install-service [--root] [--no-start] [--print]` — Install (and start) the systemd user service that runs `watch`
- `folderblog gallery [STATE] [BLOG]` — Turn the photo gallery on or off; on adds gallery/ and the gallery templates (no argument: show its state)
- `folderblog agents-md [BLOG] [--write]` — Regenerate the contract section of the blog's AGENTS.md (prints it without --write)
- `folderblog guide` — Show the step-by-step guide to everything folderblog does
- `folderblog man` — Show the guide as a manual page (piped: print the roff source, e.g. `> folderblog.1`)

## Checking your work

1. `folderblog check` — renders everything, reports template errors as `file:line`,
   validates the feed, and flags broken internal links and path collisions. Exit code 1
   on errors. Also run `folderblog check --fixtures stress` and `--fixtures empty`.
2. `folderblog preview` — http://127.0.0.1:4000 with live reload and drafts.
   `folderblog preview --fixtures stress` renders your theme against stress content:
   very long titles, no-title posts, images, bundles, code, tables, footnotes, raw HTML,
   deep tag lists, many years. Fixture sets: `empty`, `one`, `stress`. Fixtures replace only
   `posts/`, `pages/`, `drafts/` and `gallery/` (the gallery still needs `[gallery] enabled = true`); blog.toml, `[params]`, `data/` and `static/` stay yours.
   `--fixtures` also works with `build`, `check` and `data`
   (`folderblog data --fixtures stress` lists the fixture URLs). No fixture uses a custom
   layout, so render one yourself if you add `_layouts/<name>.html`.
3. `folderblog data /2024/05/hello/` — prints the exact template context for that URL as
   JSON; `folderblog data` lists every output URL and the template that renders it.
4. `folderblog build --out /tmp/site` — a full build into any folder, to inspect files.

Toolchains (Tailwind, bundlers) are optional and never required. If you want one, add
commands to `[build] pre/post` in blog.toml, not to the theme. A post-build command can
write into `$FOLDERBLOG_OUT`, e.g. `npx tailwindcss -i theme/_src/in.css -o "$FOLDERBLOG_OUT/assets/site.css" --minify`.
Pre-build commands must not write into watched folders (it would retrigger builds) unless
that path is listed in `watch.ignore`.
